title: Mortara wins a chaotic Lausitzring Race 1 as Rast rolls
dek: Edoardo Mortara won a shortened Race 1 at the Lausitzring for Mercedes from seventh on the grid, 0.920 seconds clear of Timo Glock, after a safety car, a red flag and René Rast’s violent roll.

chapters.title: A slender lead and an Audi in trouble
text: The DTM arrived at the Lausitzring on 19–20 May for the second double-header of a 20-race season, with the title fight already tight. Hockenheim had shared out the opening honours: Gary Paffett won Race 1 from pole for Mercedes, and Timo Glock took Race 2 from pole for BMW, which left Glock leading the championship by a slender margin.

Several storylines travelled east with the paddock. Philipp Eng, the Austrian BMW rookie, was only in his second race weekend. Pascal Wehrlein was back in the series with Mercedes and had been the early pace-setter in practice, while Mike Rockenfeller had been second in first practice for Audi. Audi were otherwise short of speed all weekend, and the reigning champion René Rast went into the race with a title defence that was already slipping.

The race was scheduled for 55 minutes. Every driver had to make one pit stop for fresh tyres, and a driver rejoining on cold rubber could lose a great deal of time, so the timing of that stop mattered. That combination was about to decide a race in which very little went to plan.

chapters.title: Auer snatches pole from Eng by seven thousandths
text: Conditions were dry and stable, with a cloudy sky and an air temperature of about 15 degrees. Eng set the early benchmark with 1m37.495s and held the top spot through the closing minutes, as the rest of the field collected personal-best sectors without quite beating him. Glock and Marco Wittmann moved up behind the Austrian, and Bruno Spengler and Wehrlein followed.

Lucas Auer, the Mercedes driver from Silberpfeil Energy, then delivered a 1m37.343s on his final lap to take pole by 0.007 seconds from Eng, who started from the front row for the first time in his DTM career. Spengler took third, 0.170s off the pole time, ahead of Wehrlein on 1m37.518s. Glock was fifth, 0.191s adrift, and Wittmann sixth, with Edoardo Mortara seventh and Paul di Resta eighth for Mercedes. The top ten were separated by only 0.622 seconds.

Audi’s struggles were plain. Nico Müller was the best of them in ninth, followed by Rockenfeller in tenth. Paffett could manage only 14th, with Rast 15th and Jamie Green 17th, and Daniel Juncadella, last of the 18 cars, was 1.177s off the pole time.

chapters.title: Two accidents and a sprint to the flag
text: The race was neutralised before the first lap was complete. Müller stalled on the grid from ninth place after the clutch bit more than usual, and Green, starting from the back row, had no sight of the stationary Audi and ran into its rear. Both cars were badly damaged and neither driver was hurt. Auer held the lead into the first corner despite a better launch from Eng, and Spengler took second place from the BMW rookie.

The field spent six laps behind the safety car while the debris was cleared from the start-finish straight, and the restart was staged in double file. Within moments the race was stopped again. Rast, running on the outside at Turn 8, was touched by Loïc Duval, spun across the grass and rolled, ending up without a roof. After several anxious seconds he held up a thumb through what was left of the cage. The red flag brought a long stoppage, and when the race resumed there were only about 20 minutes left to run, which turned a 55-minute race into a flat-out sprint.

chapters.title: Late stoppers jump the order
text: The second restart left Auer in front, with Spengler holding off Eng and Glock engaged in a duel with Wehrlein. With the window shortened by the stoppage, the order was decided by when each driver came in. The first group, including Spengler, Eng and di Resta, pitted in a tight bunch, and Auer and Wehrlein followed a lap later. Auer rejoined ahead of Spengler, but Wehrlein came out on cold tyres and was soon passed.

The early stoppers paid the price. Auer and Wehrlein lost time on cold rubber, finishing fourth and eighth respectively, and Spengler later said he did not think stopping so early had been ideal. Glock and then Mortara waited longer. Glock came in a lap later than he had expected and rejoined narrowly ahead of Auer, and Mortara, who stopped a lap after Glock, came back out in front of the group and found himself leading on the road. Wittmann said afterwards that one or two seconds made the difference in such a tight window, and that Mortara had made the leap forward with his stop.

chapters.title: Mortara fights back past Eng for the win
text: Eng, on tyres that were already warm, closed up within a lap and took the lead from Mortara at Turn 1, and for a while the rookie looked set for a maiden victory. He could not shake the two cars behind him, though, and with his DRS used up Mortara retook the lead with DRS down the main straight with roughly two minutes left. On the next lap Glock used his own DRS to take second from Eng in the same place.

Mortara crossed the line first after 21 laps, 0.920 seconds ahead of Glock, with Eng a further 1.967s back, 2.887s behind the winner, in third. It was Mortara’s first DTM win for Mercedes. Eng’s third place was the first podium of his DTM career, in only his third race. Auer finished fourth, 3.185s behind, with Spengler, di Resta and Wittmann next and Wehrlein, Paffett and Farfus rounding out the top ten.

For Audi the afternoon was a disaster. With Green and Müller out at the start, Rast and Duval out after the roll and only two cars finishing, the brand left without a single point. Glock’s second place stretched his championship lead to 62 points against 45 for Paffett, with Mortara third on 37.

facts.t: Win from seventh on the grid
facts.v: Edoardo Mortara won in a Mercedes-AMG after starting seventh, finishing 0.920 seconds ahead of Timo Glock and 2.887 seconds ahead of third-placed Philipp Eng.
